## Chicago Weekend Trip Snapshot

A compact 3-day plan for **May 15–17, 2026** that fits your interests in **jazz, contemporary art, and independent bookstores**, with a **walk/transit-first** approach and a target budget of **$700 total excluding airfare**.

## Weekend Itinerary and Cost Plan

| Day | Focus | Main Plan | Est. Cost |
|---|---|---|---:|
| Fri, May 15 | River North + Loop | Check in, contemporary art stop, jazz night, bookstore browse | $190 |
| Sat, May 16 | West Loop + Millennium Park | Museum-heavy day, lunch, live music, neighborhood walk | $245 |
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/5/58/Calle_E_Monroe_St%2C_Chicago%2C_Illinois%2C_Estados_Unidos%2C_2012-10-20%2C_DD_04.jpg Alt=| Sat, May 16 | West Loop + Millennium Park | Museum-heavy day, lunch, live music, neighborhood walk | $245 |, Chicago, United States
| Sun, May 17 | Hyde Park or Andersonville | Final museum/bookstore stop, relaxed brunch, depart | $155 |
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/9/9d/2_Oct1978_McDonalds_Hyde_Park_Chicago.jpg Alt=| Sun, May 17 | Hyde Park or Andersonville | Final museum/bookstore stop, relaxed brunch, depart | $155 |, Chicago, United States

### Day 1: River North Arrival + Jazz Night
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/music-note.svg
- Morning: Arrive and settle in near **River North** for easy access to downtown transit and walkable dining.
- Afternoon: Visit a contemporary art space such as the **Museum of Contemporary Art Chicago** or a nearby gallery walk.
- Evening: Catch live jazz at a club in the downtown core; finish with a short independent bookstore stop if time allows.
- Backup indoor activity: Browse a large downtown bookstore and café for a low-cost, weather-proof evening.

Estimated cost:
- Lodging share: $120
- Transit: $10
- Museum/gallery: $25
- Food/drink: $35
- Jazz cover or ticket: $40
- Total: **$230**

### Day 2: West Loop Art + Music Day
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- Morning: Start with breakfast, then head by transit to a museum or major contemporary collection.
- Afternoon: Walk the **West Loop** and nearby streets for design shops, galleries, and lunch.
- Evening: Book a second jazz set or a small venue show; keep dinner casual to stay on budget.
- Backup indoor activity: Spend extra time in a museum special exhibition or a nearby indoor market.

Estimated cost:
- Lodging share: $120
- Transit: $10
- Museum admission: $35
- Food/drink: $55
- Music ticket: $45
- Total: **$265**

### Day 3: Hyde Park or Andersonville Wind-Down
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/book.svg
- Morning: Choose **Hyde Park** for a museum-and-campus feel or **Andersonville** for bookstores and slower neighborhood browsing.
- Afternoon: Fit in one last independent bookstore, then a relaxed lunch before departure.
- Evening: Depart or keep this as a short final transit leg.
- Backup indoor activity: Coffee-and-bookstore time, or a small neighborhood museum if you want to stay indoors.

Estimated cost:
- Lodging share: $90
- Transit: $10
- Museum/bookstore stop: $15
- Food/drink: $40
- Total: **$155**

## Best Neighborhood to Stay In

### River North
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- Best fit for your trip because it is **central, walkable, and transit-friendly**.
- Easy access to downtown museums, jazz venues, and bookstore stops.
- Good balance of convenience and nightlife without needing a car.

Typical budget target:
- Mid-range hotel or well-rated room: **$140–$220 per night**
- For 3 nights, aim for **$420–$660 total** if booking carefully

## Budget Fit and Recommended Spend

- **Target trip total:** about **$650–$700**
- **Suggested split:**
  - Lodging: **$420–$520**
  - Food and drinks: **$140–$180**
  - Transit: **$30–$40**
  - Admissions and live music: **$60–$90**

Best value move:
- Stay in **River North** or the **Loop edge** and use the CTA for nearly everything.
- Prioritize **one major museum day, one jazz night, and one bookstore-heavy neighborhood stop** to keep the trip balanced and affordable.
